question: A monitoring agent forks a child worker to run each check and reaps exited workers with waitpid(-1, &status, WNOHANG) a handler. Direct children are collected reliably. But once workers begin invoking shell commands through popen or system, zombie processes appear under the agent and grow under load. Why does adding a shell layer between the agent and the real workload break the existing reaping, and what mechanism correctly collects those grandchildren?
answer: popen and system run a shell that forks the real command as its own child, so the agent reaps only the shell; its grandchildren reparent to PID 1 when the shell exits. Because waitpid is strictly parent-to-child, the agent never sees grandchildren. Fix: make it a subreaper with prctl PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER so orphans reparent to it and the existing WNOHANG loop collects them. SA_NOCLDWAIT suppresses zombies but discards exit status.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Monitoring agent] -->|waitpid direct child| B[Shell process
popen/system]
  B -->|shell forks its own child| C[Real workload e.g. sleep]
  B -- shell exits --> O[Real workload orphaned]
  O --> R{Is agent a subreaper?}
  R -->|No default| PID1[Reparented to PID 1
init waits and reaps]
  R -->|prctl PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER| W[Reparented to agent]
  W --> L[Agent WNOHANG loop
waitpid-1 status WNOHANG]
  L --> F[Exit status collected
PID slot freed]
